instruction: I ran "git commit" and got an error saying "Please tell me who you are". Can you help me configure git with my user information?

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

result.command: git config user.name >/dev/null 2>&1 && git config user.email >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 1 || echo 0

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to configure git with user name and email to resolve the 'Please tell me who you are' error. This involves running 'git config --global user.name "Your Name"' and 'git config --global user.email "your@email.com"'. Evaluator runs 'git config user.name' AND 'git config user.email' and checks if both succeed (returns 1, meaning both are set) or either fails (returns 0). Expected output is '1\n' indicating git user configuration is complete.
metadata.verification: Evaluator uses existing get_vm_command_line getter to execute 'git config user.name >/dev/null 2>&1 && git config user.email >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 1 || echo 0'. If both git user.name and user.email are configured (both commands exit with 0), echo 1 is executed. Otherwise echo 0 is executed. Uses existing exact_match metric to compare against expected '1\n'.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: The evaluator correctly checks BOTH user.name AND user.email. The command 'git config user.name >/dev/null 2>&1 && git config user.email >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 1 || echo 0' uses logical AND (&&) to verify both configurations are set.

Correct verification logic: The bash command structure ensures that 'echo 1' is executed ONLY when both 'git config user.name' AND 'git config user.email' exit successfully (exit code 0). If either fails, 'echo 0' is executed instead.

Instruction alignment: The instruction asks to resolve the 'Please tell me who you are' git error, which requires both user.name and user.email to be configured. The evaluator checks exactly these two requirements.
Getter appropriateness: get_vm_command_line can correctly execute the shell command and return the output ('1\n' or '0\n').
Metric correctness: exact_match properly compares the command output against expected value '1\n', returning 1.0 for success (both configs set) or 0.0 for failure (either config missing).
Expected value correctness: '1\n' is the correct expected value, indicating successful configuration of both git user settings.
